q: A senior streams two conductors' recordings of the same symphony and attends a live performance, then writes which interpretation best honors the score. She is doing what?
o: Evaluating exemplary musical examples across media

q: Which comment shows an evaluation of a live performance?
o: The woodwinds' unified attacks gave the finale real clarity

q: A fugue in which voices enter one after another with the same subject displays which advanced texture?
e: Fugal entries are imitative and polyphonic.

q: Heterophony occurs when performers do what?
o: Play slightly varied versions of the same melody at the same time
e: Heterophony is simultaneous variation of one melody.

q: A dominant seventh chord built on G contains which pitches?
e: A dominant seventh has a major triad and a minor seventh.

q: An inverted chord is one in which what is true?
o: A note other than the root is in the bass

q: A passage shifts between 3/4 and 6/8 so that the measure length stays similar but the feel changes. This technique is called what?
e: Hemiola shifts between two-feel and three-feel groupings.

q: Analyzing a polyrhythm means studying what?
o: Two or more contrasting rhythms sounding together

q: A theme and variations piece develops its ideas by doing what?
o: Restating the theme with changing treatments

q: In sonata-allegro form, the section that presents the main themes is called the ___.
An ensemble tunes its chord so the root, third and fifth are balanced, and the voices sound as one. Which two concepts are being analyzed?
e: Balance is volume; blend is tone unity.

q: Poor blend in a choir is often caused by what?
o: Singers using widely different vowel shapes and vibrato

q: A choral work from the Renaissance with sacred Latin text and imitative polyphony is a ___.
Which genre is most associated with sectional large-scale orchestral works in several movements?
e: A symphony is a multi-movement orchestral piece.

q: Analyzing how a composer uses dissonance resolving to consonance addresses which element?
Expression in music is shaped by which of these?
A musician with a sore wrist should do what first?
o: Stop playing and consult a qualified health professional if pain persists

q: Which routine best applies wellness to a long practice day?
o: Breaks, hydration, stretching and varied tasks
e: A varied, restful routine protects the body.

q: A student notates a melody with triplets across the bar line and a tied note into the next measure. What must the notation show?
o: Accurate durations and pitch with ties

q: When writing a melody in compound meter, how should eighth notes in 6/8 usually be beamed?
The term rubato directs a performer to do what?
The expression sostenuto asks for what?
A tenor adapts his tone from bright for a musical-theatre piece to a darker, rounder sound for a sacred work. This shows what?
Which approach best develops mature tone on a brass instrument?
o: Long tones with a steady airstream and open throat

q: A pianist analyzes how arm weight and wrist freedom affect her sound and reduces tension. She is doing what?
o: Applying psychomotor and kinesthetic analysis to technique

q: A singer feels her breath gets shallow on high phrases. What is the best adjustment?
o: Re-engage low breath support and keep the ribs expanded
e: Support remains steady on high notes.

q: Playing a passage of mixed triplets and sixteenth notes at tempo requires what?
To master a difficult rhythm, a student should first do what?
o: Play it at full speed immediately
Practice slowly with a metronome and increase gradually

q: A piece in F-sharp minor has how many sharps in its key signature?
e: F-sharp minor shares A major's three sharps.

q: A modulation to the dominant key adds what to the key signature of a major piece, in general?
o: One more sharp or one fewer flat
e: Moving to the dominant adds a sharp.

q: Just intonation adjusts a major third to be slightly lower than equal temperament so the chord rings. Why?
o: To make the chord resonate purely

q: A conductor asks for a long-arching phrase that peaks in measure six. What does she want?
o: Direction in the phrase with a planned climax
e: Phrasing builds to a high point.

q: A student writes a four-part arrangement for her ensemble with increasingly demanding rhythms. She is doing what?
o: Creating music at an increasing level of difficulty

q: Which tool allows a composer to hear a notated draft before the ensemble rehearses it?
A hornist sight reads a piece in a new style and still produces a centered, appropriate sound. This shows what?
What most helps a sight reader preserve tone quality at tempo?
A sight-reading violist scans ahead for position shifts and plans her bow distribution. She is refining what?
Why should a sight reader keep a loose grip and open posture?
o: To maintain tone and avoid strain

q: A sight reader finds a measure with sixteenth-note groupings and slurred pairs. What should she prioritize?
Which method keeps a sight reader in time during a change of meter?
o: Counting the new pattern aloud with a steady subdivision

q: A sight-reading piece modulates up a whole step in the middle section. What should the reader check?
When a piece shifts between Dorian and Aeolian mode, which note usually changes?
A singer reading an unfamiliar line uses movable do to label scale degrees. What is that tool?
e: Movable do is a pitch system.

q: Which method helps an instrumentalist read pitches in a new key?
o: Labeling note names or scale degrees mentally

q: A sight reader sees a forte-piano marking followed by a swell. How should she respond?
o: Start loud, drop to soft, then grow

q: What is the benefit of identifying phrase peaks before sight reading?
o: It helps shape the line musically

q: An alto matches her vowel to the sopranos' open 'ah' on a held chord and tunes the third. She is working on what?
Why do ensembles tune the third of a chord lower in just intonation?
o: To reduce beating and ring more purely

q: A student hears a piece with ostinato, modal harmonies and a gamelan-like texture and identifies its cultural origin. She is doing what?
o: Discriminating music by culture and style

q: Which feature would help distinguish Classical period music from Romantic?
o: Balanced phrases and clear forms versus expansive expression

q: A student evaluates how protest songs influenced a social movement. She is evaluating what?
o: The relevance of music to society

q: Why do many cultures use music in rites of passage?
o: It marks transitions and expresses shared values

q: Using ratios to explain why an octave sounds consonant connects music with which subject?
Setting a poem's meter to rhythm connects music with which discipline?
e: Poetic meter links to musical rhythm.

q: A music therapist uses songs to support patients' communication. Which career field is this?
e: Music therapy is a music-related career.

q: Explaining a music career includes describing what?
o: Typical duties, training and work settings
e: Careers are explained by duties and training.

q: Evaluating how AI-generated music affects composers addresses which area?
e: AI raises several issues for musicians.

q: Why is crediting composers and performers important?
o: It respects creators and supports their livelihoods

q: A senior builds a curriculum vitae and audition video for conservatory applications. What is she generating?
o: Tools for college and career preparation

q: Which item is typical of an electronic music portfolio?
o: Recordings, repertoire list and teacher references

q: During a recorded performance review, the best audience behavior is what?
o: Listening attentively and respecting the performers' work

q: A performer who handles a mistake onstage with composure is showing what?
A rubric for evaluating a mariachi ensemble differs from one for a madrigal group because each style prizes what?
o: Different tone, rhythm and stylistic features

q: Which is the best criterion for evaluating a choral performance?
A peer's feedback names a specific measure and suggests a new bowing. What type of feedback is this?
Feedback can be shared in which formats?
A musician logs each rehearsal's goals, listens to recordings and adjusts her plan weekly. She is developing what?
Which tool best supports personal artistic improvement?
o: Recorded self-assessments tied to specific goals
e: Tools tied to goals show progress.

q: A composer compares her new piece with a model work and notes how the model develops its motif more fully. She is doing what?
o: Evaluating a composition by comparing it to an exemplary model
Copying the model note for note

q: After evaluating a performance against a model, which recommendation is most useful?
o: Adjust the balance in measures 12 to 16 so the melody leads
